headline: Russia is exploring the integration of heavy air-to-surface and anti-ship missiles onto its Su-30 fighter family, according to Kommersant. Oleg Pankov, Chief Designer of the Sukhoi Design Bureau, confirmed that integration studies are underway, requiring only minor structural modifications. Neither the missile type nor the intended customer was disclosed. One possible precedent is the Russian-Indian BrahMos-A, a roughly 2.5-tonne supersonic cruise missile already integrated onto India's Su-30MKI. However, CAST Director Ruslan Pukhov believes the project could involve entirely new Russian weapons rather than derivatives of the P-800 Oniks/Yakhont.

headline: The US is delaying the transfer of 60 Patriot missiles to Ukraine. Kyiv was due to receive 8 PAC-3 missiles in September, 10 in October, another 10 in November and 12 in December. The transfer of an additional 20 PAC-2 missiles also requires Pentagon approval, despite the deliveries being funded by European countries. Dang, that's extremely low. The US has its own stockpile shortages to deal with, and although it's trying to ramp up production, that will take time. I think Ukraine would be much better off relying more on European alternatives that it already operates, such as IRIS-T SLM and SAMP/T, rather than waiting for just 10 PAC-3 missiles a month. Those could be used up in a single hour during a major Russian missile attack. At some point, you have to accept that Iskander-Ms will get through and save the interceptors for other incoming threats.
